title: 5 ways brand lift studies can inform your campaign strategy

facts.fact: The StackAdapt blog article '5 ways brand lift studies can inform your campaign strategy' was published on 2021-12-13.
StackAdapt's example upper-funnel brand lift question asks whether a user recalls seeing an ad for the brand in the last 14 days.
facts.quote: whether a user recalls seeing an ad for the brand in question in the last 14 days

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that a brand lift study measures the impact of campaigns across all of an advertiser's programmatic channels.
facts.quote: A brand lift study measures the impact of your campaigns across all your programmatic channels.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that brand lift studies usually revolve around a survey, with an 'exposed' group that has seen the ad and a 'control' group that has not.
facts.quote: Your “exposed” group is a group of users who have seen your ad in the past, and your “control” group is a group of users who have not seen your ad.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that survey ads (also called discovery ads or brand lift ads) use an HTML5 format to create an interactive unit for users.
facts.quote: Survey ads use an HTML5 format to create an interactive unit for users.

facts.fact: StackAdapt lists brand awareness, ad recall, brand favourability and brand affinity as metrics a brand lift study shows for incrementality.
facts.quote: Brand lift will show you incrementality through metrics like brand awareness, ad recall, brand favourability, and brand affinity.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that brand lift studies can measure upper-funnel campaigns' impact on brand perception and mid- to lower-funnel campaigns' impact on consideration or purchase intent.
facts.quote: It can be used to measure the impact of upper funnel campaigns on your consumers’ perception of your brand, but it’s also effective when it comes to mid- to lower funnel campaigns, for measuring consideration or purchase intent.
